name: Intercompany Consolidation
title: Intercompany Consolidation
answer: Intercompany consolidation is the process of combining the financial results of separate legal entities under common control into one set of statements, eliminating internal transactions, balances, and unrealized profits. In an AI accounting context, the scope includes automating elimination entries, matching intercompany invoices and loans, reconciling transfer pricing, and producing consolidated trial balances across multiple currencies and accounting standards. It covers both statutory consolidation and management reporting for groups.

sections.body: Intercompany consolidation is the process of combining the financial results of separate legal entities under common control into one set of statements, eliminating internal transactions, balances, and unrealized profits. It covers both statutory consolidation and management reporting for groups.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: AI consolidation tools typically run on cloud financial consolidation platforms or ERP add-ons that connect to the general ledgers of each subsidiary. They rely on a central data lake or warehouse where intercompany transaction data is standardized, often with APIs pulling from SAP, Oracle, NetSuite, or similar systems. Compute is modest compared to large language models, as most work is rule-based matching and anomaly detection on structured tables, with some use of small machine learning models for classification.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The system first maps each entity's chart of accounts to a group chart, then identifies intercompany pairs by matching invoice numbers, amounts, counterparty codes, and dates. Machine learning classifiers flag likely eliminations and propose journal entries, while deterministic rules handle currency translation and ownership percentages. Human accountants review and approve proposed adjustments, and the system learns from corrections to improve future matching.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Consolidation involves sensitive financial data, so access controls, audit trails, and data lineage are critical. AI-generated elimination entries must be explainable, with clear links to source transactions and the matching logic used. Risks include incorrect elimination of third-party transactions, misstated minority interests, and regulatory noncompliance if the system is not validated under applicable accounting standards such as IFRS 10 or ASC 810. Ownership of the AI model and responsibility for final statements remains with the finance team and external auditors.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Consolidation is moving toward continuous close, where intercompany differences are flagged daily rather than at period end. Generative AI may draft elimination memos and footnote disclosures from structured data, while graph-based models could map complex ownership chains and joint arrangements more accurately. Over time, systems may handle real-time consolidation for multinational groups with hundreds of entities, reducing manual reconciliation to exception handling only.
